extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and their representatives (patent prosecutors/agents/attorneys) preparing for USPTO examiner interviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applicants and practitioners on when and how to request, prepare for, conduct, and follow up on interviews with USPTO examiners to advance prosecution. Covers timing, preparation, in-interview conduct, strategy options, relationship management, and post-interview documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing & advance submission for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Most interviews occur after a non-final office action; applicants should prepare and schedule in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit an agenda and any proposed claim amendments at least 24 hours prior to the interview. Propose interview dates at least 5 days out (per USPTO automated interview request form). Interviews are most effective when the application is top of mind with the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough preparation of merits and prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully review the rejections and prior art cited by the examiner and ensure arguments/amendments are viable in light of the full cited references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look beyond the specific passages cited by the examiner — make sure arguments/amendments are not foreclosed by other disclosure in the cited prior art. Especially review the rejections and all relevant parts of cited references before the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator of examiner behavior and analogous cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Research the examiner's past decisions and how similar issues were addressed in other cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research the examiner's statistics and recent cases addressing similar issues. Especially for §101 rejections, see what types of arguments and amendments other applicants used to persuade the same examiner. Use Patent Examiner Statistics websites (e.g., Patent Bots, Juristat) to inform strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective interview conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure and conduct the interview as a focused, cooperative discussion respecting time limits and seeking solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal interview lasts no more than 30 minutes. View the interview as a two-way discussion rather than an argument. Don't just highlight disagreements — provide potential solutions. Actively listen to the examiner's comments, ask clarifying questions, and be receptive to suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer multiple options and pursue a joint hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide alternative approaches and collaborate with the examiner to find an agreeable path to allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple Options: Give the examiner different strategy options (e.g., different proposed claim amendments). This gives the examiner an opportunity to determine which approach would likely work best. Joint Hypothesis: Find a 'yes' path together by jointly identifying workable changes or arguments that address the examiner's concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect examiner constraints and practicalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize examiners' production quotas and practical incentives when proposing solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect for Examiner's Constraints: Examiners have production quotas; offering allowable subject matter helps both sides. Tailor proposals to what the examiner can reasonably accept and process within their constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professionalism and build relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Be courteous and respectful to maintain a good working relationship with the examiner and improve chances of favorable outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being courteous and respectful to the examiner, especially when disagreements arise, is crucial to maintaining a good relationship and reaching a favorable outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-interview documentation and confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and confirm the substance of the interview in writing per USPTO practice and regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner records an Interview Summary in the file wrapper. Applicant must file an Interview Summary identifying topics discussed (37 CFR 1.133). Substance of agreements should be confirmed in writing to ensure the record reflects any understandings or commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: When not to request an interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid interviews in situations where they are unlikely to be productive or appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request an interview when the issues are purely formal (e.g., drawing objections). Avoid requesting an interview after Final unless requesting AFCP 2.0. Also do not request an interview when the examiner has not yet substantively examined the case.
